title: Scalar tensor resolutions compute the recorded sheaf derived tensor
statement: For a small site J, a commutative ring A, an A_J-algebra sheaf R flat over A_J [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], and arbitrary A-modules P,Q, let F be the canonical realization [def-sfb-flat-scalar-realization]. The recorded derived tensor F(P)[0]⊗ᴸ_R F(Q)[0] [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] is isomorphic to the localization of F applied termwise to the scalar projective resolution of P tensored with Q, reindexed from chain degree n to cochain degree -n. No DVR or finiteness hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tags 06YQ (bounded flat K-flat), 06YP (K-flat quasi-isomorphism) and 06YU (derived Tor)

proof.text: Realize the scalar projective resolution and its augmentation. Exactness carries the augmentation to a quasi-isomorphism. Projective scalar modules are flat, and canonical realization preserves flatness. Its cochain extension is nonpositive, so the independent-universe bounded-flat theorem gives K-flatness.

Resolve the degree-zero realization of Q by the proved independent-coefficient K-flat resolution theorem. The total-tensor comparison computes the recorded derived tensor on both K-flat resolutions. The realized scalar resolution is also categorically K-flat by the bounded-above flat theorem. Its left-tensor clause preserves the second augmentation, removing the second resolution after localization. The degree-zero single comparison then identifies the total complex with termwise right tensor.

Apply the ordinary scalar tensor natural isomorphism termwise to the scalar cochain resolution. Commuting the scalar tensor functor with extension along n↦-n identifies the resulting complex with the displayed reindexed scalar tensor resolution. Localize these chain isomorphisms.
